answer: A Pedersen commitment hides a value as g to the power v times h to the power r, binding the prover while revealing nothing until the opening is shown, so the hidden value cannot be swapped after the fact. A lone agent may wander through many fresh identities, yet each one still needs a distinct random blinding factor and a matching opening, and the meadow of fake accounts collapses when openings are checked against the same committed value, because at its nadir a farm has no shortcut to forge a second opening for a different value.
